property_summary: For any valid transfer where all sub-calls succeed without reverting, the correct contract returns true, but the mutant returns false.

For any call to 'transfer' with a valid token-contract address that does not revert (i.e., all internal calls succeed), the function must return true; the mutant incorrectly returns false even on success.
For any admissible input where the external contract at 'contract_address' does not revert on any sub-call, C.transfer must return true; the mutant incorrectly returns false.

For any admissible input where the external contract at 'contract_address' is an EOA or an adversarial helper that does not revert on the sub-calls, C.transfer must return true because all requires pass and external calls succeed; the mutant returns false.

The reference C.transfer always returns true when all internal calls succeed, while the buggy version always returns false under the same successful conditions, violating the invariant that a non-reverting transfer call returns true.
The reference contract reverts the entire transaction if any internal transferFrom call fails, while the mutant does not revert and returns true even if some transfers fail.

For any call to transfer with non-empty arrays where the caller has sufficient allowance at the given contract_address, the reference ensures tos.length equals vs.length, causing array-mismatch calls to revert; the buggy version skips this check and proceeds with iteration over tos.length, reading out-of-bounds from vs when vs is shorter, which leads to a revert from the external call or zero-value transfer that would have been prevented, violating the invariant that such mismatched calls always fail on the length check.

The reference function always executes exactly tos.length iterations (never an out-of-bounds access on tos), while the buggy version may index out of bounds in tos when tos.length < vs.length, causing either a revert or a discrepancy in the number of successful external calls.

For any valid input, the reference C always returns true without reverting; the buggy version can revert due to an out-of-bounds array access when vs.length differs from tos.length (despite the earlier equality check).

The reference always completes without reverting and returns true for any input where tos.length equals vs.length, while the buggy version reverts whenever vs.length differs from tos.length (due to the equality check removal) instead of reverting from the equality check.

For any input where the arrays are equal length, both versions iterate the same number of times, but the buggy version uses vs.length as the loop bound and will index out of bounds on tos when vs.length > tos.length, causing a revert instead of returning true.

For any input where tos.length equals vs.length, the reference always completes the full number of external calls equal to tos.length, while the buggy version may iterate beyond tos bounds when vs.length differs, causing a revert that prevents the same number of successful calls.

In the reference, the transfer function calls 'transferFrom(address,address,uint256)' on the target contract, debiting from msg.sender; in the buggy version, it calls 'transfer(address,uint256)' which debits from the target contract itself, so when calling into a contract with both functions, the reference reverts (due to allowance/balance issues) while the buggy one succeeds, or vice versa.
A call to transfer with contract_address == address(c) must always revert in the reference, but succeeds in the mutant, so the presence of a revert distinguishes them.

For any call to transfer with contract_address equal to the contract itself, the reference always reverts due to the validAddress modifier, while the mutant allows the call to proceed, causing a change in the return value or state.
For any call to transfer where contract_address equals address(c), the reference always reverts, but the mutant proceeds without revert.
For any call to transfer where contract_address equals address(c), the correct contract always reverts, while the mutant proceeds without revert.
